title: Fecal microbiota transplantation for primary sclerosing cholangitis - randomized study versus sham transplantation (FMT-SCLER).
official: Fecal microbiota transplantation for primary sclerosing cholangitis - randomized study versus sham transplantation (FMT-SCLER).
summary: Main objective: To assess in patients with PSC the efficacy of FMT versus sham transplantation on ALP and bilirubin at week 48 (surrogate markers of transplantation-free survival in PSC patients) in addition to standard UDCA therapy.

interventions.name: Double encapsulated oral transplant of fecal microbiota

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Males or females
2. Subject affiliated to the French Social Security System
3. Age ≥18 and ≤75 years
4. Large duct PSC verified by retrograde, operative, percutaneous or magnetic resonance cholangiography (MRC) demonstrating intrahepatic and /or extrahepatic biliary duct changes consistent with PSC
5. IBD diagnosed according to international guidelines (presence of endoscopic and histologic signs)
6. IBD inactive for at least 6 months (defined by no evidence of flare and no change in treatment)
7. ALP ≥ 1.3 ULN (at least 2 times within a 3 months pre-inclusion period) or elevated total bilirubin ≤50mol/l (with concomitant elevated direct bilirubin).
8. Treatment with UDCA (13-23 mg/kg/d) for at least 6 months and at the same dosage for at least 3 months
9. Using contraceptive in women of childbearing potential. Women of childbearing potential, i.e. fertile, following menarche and until becoming post-menopaused unless permanently sterile, who are sexually active have to apply a highly effective method of birth control with a low failure rate (i.e. less than 1% per year) when used constantly and correctly.
10. Written informed consent signed
Exclusion criteria:
1. Small duct PSC
2. History of acute cholangitis in the last 3 months prior to inclusion or current acute cholangitis
3. HIV infection
4. Prior liver transplantation
5. Endoscopic treatment for bile duct stenosis ≤ 3 months prior to inclusion or planned within 3 months post randomization date
6. History of or established or suspected hepatobiliary carcinoma.
7. Any severe comorbidity that may reduce life expectancy
8. History of malignancy diagnosed or treated within 2 years (recent localized treatment of squamous or non-invasive basal skin cancers is permitted; cervical carcinoma in situ is allowed if appropriately treated prior to inclusion)
9. Dosage changes of treatment for liver disease in the last 3 months or new treatment for liver disease started in the last 3 months
10. History of colorectal carcinoma or high-grade dypsplasia in previous screening colonoscopy
11. History of total colectomy
12. Autoimmune hepatitis defined by the presence of moderate to severe interface hepatitis documented on liver biopsy and at least 1 of the 2 following criteria: AST or ALT > 5 ULN, Positive anti smooth muscle auto antibodies or serum IgG > 1.5 ULN
13. Current active IBD defined by a partial Mayo score > 2 in patients with ulcerative colitis (UC), unclassed colitis or a Crohn’s Disease Activity Index (CDAI) > 150 in patients with Crohn’s disease
14. Changes in IBD treatment or initiation of a new treatment for IBD in the last 3 months
15. Current treatment with biologics (anti-TNF agent, vedolizumab, ustekinumab) or JAK inhibitors (tofacitinnib) or prednisone > 10 mg/day or budesonide > 3 mg /day) (or treatment initiated less than one month)
16. Any contra-indication to swallow capsules
17. Renal insufficiency (clearance<60 ml/min)
18. Unable to consent, subject to legal or administrative decision (protection measure or deprivation of liberty) or involuntary psychiatric care.
19. Inclusion in another clinical trial on medicinal products, clinical investigation protocol concerning a medical device or interventional protocol not concerning a health product, or in the exclusion period any other interventional study
20. Pregnancy or desire for pregnancy or breastfeeding
21. Secondary sclerosing cholangitis (notably IgG4-associated cholangitis)
22. Cirrhosis defined by Liver elastometry >14.4 kPa or by current or past decompensation of cirrhosis
23. AST or ALT > 7 ULN in the last 3 months
24. Platelets count in the last 3 months < 100 000/mm3
25. Albumin in the last 3 months <35g/L
26. Prothrombin index in the last 3 months < 70%
27. Hepatic comorbidity: HBV infection (defined by positive Ag HBS), HCV infection (defined by positive HCV RNA), alcohol abuse (defined by alcohol intake > 30g/day), metabolic dysfunction associated steatohepatitis, primary biliary cholangitis, Hemochromatosis, Wilson disease, α1-antitrypsin deficiency, celiac disease
